newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Air overflights more profitable for Russia in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Air overflights more profitable for Russia in 1996.

text.p: Russia opened 74 new air traffic corridors across its territory in 1996, boosting revenues from increased air traffic over the country, a senior Federal Aviation Service (FAS) said on Wednesday.
"These corridors allowed us to increase aircraft traffic across Russia 15 to 20 per cent compared to 1995," said Viktor Galkin, the FAS deputy director.
The new network of corridors had a total length of 11,600 km (7,250 miles), including 42 international air corridors with a total length of 5,090 km (3,700 miles), Galkin said.

He also said that Russia boosted its revenue by allowing foreign airlines to operate more flights between Europe and the Far East. The most profitable corridors are above Siberia and the northern polar region.
"Russia makes about $80 million annually for Western carriers using them," he said.
Under communism, Moscow was far more reluctant to allow foreign carriers to overfly the country, but in recent years Russia has begun to realise the commercial potential of such routes.
More air traffic corridors are likely to open in 1997, but Galkin said the exact number would depend on the demand from airlines.
